defects.description: AC-5 requires special / SQL-like characters in the search term to be treated as literal text (HTTP 200 success envelope, no DB error leaked). The AUT concatenates the term into a SQL query, so a term containing a single apostrophe breaks the query and the endpoint returns HTTP 500 with a SQLite engine error message instead of a success envelope.
defects.evidence: GET /rest/products/search?q=O'Brien (apostrophe url-encoded) -> HTTP 500, HTML body titled "Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near \"Brien\": syntax error". Reproduced twice. Contrast: q=x and q=test)) each return HTTP 200 {"status":"success","data":[]}, so only SQL-significant input (the apostrophe) triggers the failure, confirming string concatenation into SQL.

traps: AC-2/AC-1 are MET and easy to false-positive as failures: search matches the term in NAME OR DESCRIPTION (e.g. q=classic returns Apple Juice and Pomegranate Drink via description; q=apple returns Pineapple Juice). An evaluator that assumes name-only matching may wrongly flag AC-2.

AC-5 is the only real deviation. A careless evaluator might test only <, >, or unbalanced brackets (which the AUT tolerates with HTTP 200) and wrongly conclude AC-5 passes. The apostrophe is the input that exposes it.

The empty-state mock-up (AC-4) uses 'apple' only as an illustrative term; searching 'apple' actually returns 3 products. The AC is about the no-match state for ANY term (use a nonsense term like 'zzznomatchqa'). Do not treat the mock's example term as a contradiction.
Welcome banner and cookie dialog overlay the page on first load; UI assertions must dismiss them first.
The data reset on restart changes review _id values and could change product ids; AC-6 only relies on product 1 having reviews and on shape, which is stable across resets.
add-to-basket / price glyph: price is shown as e.g. '1.99¤' with a placeholder currency char; matching on a currency symbol will fail.
expectations: AC-1 MET: /#/search?q=apple lists product cards (Apple Juice, Apple Pomace, Pineapple Juice) each with name, price and 'Add to Basket'; header 'Search Results - apple'.
AC-2 MET: GET /rest/products/search?q=apple -> 200 {status:success,data:[...]}; q=zzznomatchqa -> 200 empty data.
AC-3 MET: UI results grid is populated from the same search endpoint; the displayed name set matches the API name set for the same term.
AC-4 MET: no-match search shows 'Search Results - <term>', 'No results found', 'Try adjusting your search to find what you're looking for.', and '0 of 0'.
AC-6 MET: GET /rest/products/1/reviews -> 200 {status:success,data:[...]} with message+author fields; non-empty for product 1.
Overall FAIL because AC-5 (a security acceptance criterion) is not satisfied by the live AUT.
